subsystems.name: Photometric monitor
subsystems.role: stares at the same patch of sky for months or years, recording the star's brightness every few minutes.
parts: space telescope with a wide field of view

subsystems.name: Timing extractor
subsystems.role: finds each transit and pins down its mid-point to within seconds.

subsystems.name: Residual analyser
subsystems.role: subtracts the expected clockwork and looks at what is left over.

subsystems.name: Dynamical fitter
subsystems.role: simulates the gravitational dance of the whole system and matches it to the data.

subsystems.name: Follow-up spectrograph
subsystems.role: measures the star's radial-velocity wobble to weigh the planets and break degeneracies in the timing fit.

buildSteps.title: Stare at the star
buildSteps.detail: A space telescope observes the target field almost continuously, so transits are never missed between observing seasons.

buildSteps.title: Clean the light curve
buildSteps.detail: Instrumental drifts, telescope pointing changes and the star's own pulsations are removed without erasing real transits.

buildSteps.title: Measure transit times
buildSteps.detail: For every transit, the dip's shape is fitted and its mid-point recorded, together with a realistic error bar.

buildSteps.title: Build the O−C diagram
buildSteps.detail: Each measured time is compared with a perfect, constant-period prediction; the differences are the raw signal.

buildSteps.title: Search for a pattern
buildSteps.detail: Periodograms and dynamical reasoning test whether the residuals are periodic, drifting, or chaotic.

buildSteps.title: Fit a full dynamical model
buildSteps.detail: An N-body simulation of all planets is run many times and compared with the timings until the unseen companion's mass, period and eccentricity are pinned down.

buildSteps.title: Weigh and confirm
buildSteps.detail: Radial-velocity measurements or additional transits from a second observatory confirm the companion is real and not a data artefact.

buildSteps.title: Test the architecture
buildSteps.detail: The fitted system is integrated far into the future and past to check it is stable and that the solution is physically plausible.

prerequisites.why: the signal is subtle, so years of uninterrupted timing measurements are needed to build it up.

prerequisites.tech: Sub-minute photometric precision on bright stars
prerequisites.why: timing errors of seconds translate into detectable mass limits only when the photometry is very clean.

prerequisites.tech: Fast N-body integrators and sampling algorithms
prerequisites.why: millions of trial systems must be simulated to fit the timing residuals.
the size and orbit of the planets are scaled from the star, so its properties must be known accurately.
it independently confirms the hidden planet and breaks degeneracies that timing alone leaves open.

pathway.milestone: routine use on Kepler, K2 and TESS light curves to reveal non-transiting and near-resonant planets
pathway.unlocks: fuller pictures of planetary systems that looked single-planet in the raw photometry.

pathway.milestone: longer baselines and brighter targets from ground-based survey networks and extended space missions
pathway.unlocks: lower-mass hidden planets and follow-up spectroscopy for many more systems.

pathway.milestone: application to the brightest, nearest stars with dedicated transit surveys
pathway.unlocks: mass measurements for small planets, including those in habitable zones.

pathway.milestone: timing searches for moons, rings and slow orbital decay
pathway.unlocks: probing the fine structure and long-term evolution of planetary systems.
